notes: Single-file editorial site on how towns, railways and governments agreed on a shared clock. Three built interactives: a longitude explorer showing where solar noon falls against a clock, a scrubbable timeline of milestones, and a two-question quiz with feedback. Also a glossary reached through inline links, sticky chapter navigation with scroll progress, and procedural SVG art whose marker follows the explorer. Historical facts are drawn from standard histories named on the page; dates are the commonly reported ones. The explorer uses mean solar time and ignores the equation of time, so it is an illustration rather than survey data. Limitations: the text is shorter than a full long-form publication, imagery is generated SVG only, and the layout has not been viewed in a live browser. Test status: the inline script was checked for syntax with a parser only; nothing was run or rendered in a browser.
